sense: public life, the business of the state

evidence: Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.11.3: quod ad rem pūblicam attinet
terms.comment: Latin has no separate word for politics: it is the business of the state itself. To go into politics is rem pūblicam capessere (Nep. Them. 2.1; M-O) or Traupman’s rem pūblicam inīre; to be in politics, in rē pūblicā versārī (Traupman 22, 180). For “political”, see political.

terms.latin: rēs cīvīlēs, rērum cīvīlium f. pl.
evidence: Tac. H. 2.5: cīvīlium rērum perītus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Public business as against war or private life (Lewis & Short, s.v. cīvīlis).

terms.gloss: politics as the pursuit of office: canvassing
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.1: forēnsium rērum labor et ambitiōnis occupātiō
terms.comment: The going round for votes, and so the business of seeking office; also ambition and the courting of favour in general (Lewis & Short). Bribery at elections is ambitus (Traupman 178).

phrases.latin: quod ad rem pūblicam attinet, in ūnam causam omnis contentiō conlēcta est, dē prōvinciīs
phrases.english: as far as politics goes, the whole struggle has come down to one question, the provinces

phrases.latin: nunc agilis fīō et mersor cīvīlibus undīs
phrases.english: now I turn man of action and plunge into the waves of politics

phrases.latin: prīmus autem gradus fuit capessendae reī pūblicae bellō Corcȳraeō
phrases.english: the first step of his political career came in the war with Corcyra

phrases.latin: Tūne vīs versārī aliquandō in rē pūblicā?
phrases.english: Do you want to be involved in politics some day?
a political career (literally, the course of offices)
